newsitem.title: USA: Virginia governor proposes expanding school debt.
newsitem.headline: Virginia governor proposes expanding school debt.

text.p: Virginia Gov. George Allen has proposed raising the debt authorization for local school district general obligation bonds issued via the Virgina Public School Authority, the Times-Dispatch reported.

School districts have issued $650 million of GO bonds through the authority since it was established in 1991 to help finance school construction, renovation and equipment. The legislature set a cap of $800 million.

Allen said his plan could generate an additional $1 billion for local school boards during the next five years. The Republican governor's proposal would have to be approved by the Democrat-controlled General Assembly.
State officials estimated school construction needs at $6.3 billion and said 60 percent of Virginia schools are dilapidated.

Frank Barham, executive director of the Virginia School Board Association, told the newspaper that Allen's proposal would require more funding at the state level in order to help school districts repay the higher debt.
